title: Paint App
description: Build a drawing app with a pixel grid canvas, brush tools, shape drawing, and ASCII art rendering.

Each cell value is a string like 'white', 'black', 'red', etc.
Initialize as: Array(height).fill(null).map(() => Array(width).fill('white'))

steps.description: Write a `setPixel` function that takes `x`, `y`, and `color` parameters and sets the cell at `(x, y)` to the given color. Log the updated pixel.
hints: Access the cell: canvas[y][x] (y is row, x is column)
Add bounds checking: if x < 0 || x >= width || y < 0 || y >= height
Log: 'Set pixel at (' + x + ', ' + y + ') to ' + color

verification.failureMessage: setPixel(2, 2, 'red') should set canvas[2][2] to 'red' and setPixel(0, 0, 'blue') should set canvas[0][0] to 'blue'.

If out of bounds, return null or an error message
Test by setting a pixel then reading it back

hints: Add a brushSize variable: let brushSize = 1
In the brush-aware setPixel, loop from -brushSize/2 to brushSize/2
Draw a square of pixels centered on (x, y) when brushSize > 1

steps.title: Render canvas as ASCII art
steps.description: Write a `renderCanvas` function that converts the canvas grid to an ASCII art string. Use `#` for non-white pixels and ` ` for white pixels. Log the full string row by row.
hints: Map each cell: pixel === 'white' ? ' ' : '#'
Join cells in a row with spaces: row.map(c => ...).join(' ')
Join rows with newlines for the final string

verification.successMessage: Canvas renders as ASCII art with # for colored pixels and spaces for white!
